text: dsh-model-proxy（DSH 网页端插件）：按模型 API 域名和代理模式路由请求，让指定模型服务经系统代理、自定义 HTTP/SOCKS 代理或代理链访问，其余请求保持直连。它接入 DSH 的 fetch 请求层，并提供可热更新的设置页和状态诊断。主要功能包括按域名或 provider 选择出口、内置模型域名规则、系统代理及代理链配置、查看路由状态与测试代理。适合需要为不同模型 API 配置网络出口的 DSH 用户。需要可用的代理出口；无需额外 API Key。

dsh-model-proxy routes DSH model API requests by domain through system, HTTP/SOCKS, or chained proxies, leaving others direct. Settings update live and show routing status and connectivity. Configure domain or provider rules; proxied traffic needs an available proxy, with no extra API key.
想让 DSH 的模型 API 请求按域名走不同代理。
DSH 能否只把 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 请求发到代理？
我想让国内模型直连、海外模型通过代理访问。
怎样让模型请求使用 Windows 系统代理？
我需要为 DSH 配置 SOCKS 代理或多级代理链。
希望在设置页切换代理模式后不用重启就生效。
How can I route selected model API domains through a proxy in DSH?
I want DSH to follow my system proxy for model requests.
DSH Model Proxy 的功能「域名路由」：按主机匹配规则选择代理出口或直连。默认规则可将常见海外模型 API 经代理，并让配置的直连域名保持直连。
DSH Model Proxy 的功能「代理模式」：可选择规则、系统、自定义或关闭模式；自定义出口支持 HTTP 与 SOCKS 协议，并能配置多个代理跳点。
DSH Model Proxy 的功能「热更新设置」：在 DSH 设置页修改代理模式、地址和域名规则后，插件监听设置更新并重新启用路由，无需重启。
DSH Model Proxy 的功能「状态诊断」：设置页可查看路由状态，并发起代理连通性检查；插件通过同源诊断路由返回检查状态。
dsh-model-proxy 通过 fetch 包装路由请求；未经过 fetch 的传输方式（例如原生 WebSocket）不会由此路由层处理。

dsh-model-proxy README · dsh-model-proxy：English | [中文](README_zh.md)

Route DeepSeek Harness **model API requests** through a proxy so third-party overseas
model providers work from mainland China, while **requests outside the domains you list stay
direct** — web search, page fetching, MCP servers and tool calls are not proxied unless you
add their domains.

dsh-model-proxy README · dsh-model-proxy：- Does not patch any harness file; uninstalling restores the original behaviour exactly
- **System proxy**, **custom proxy** (`http` / `https` / `socks4` / `socks4a` / `socks5` / `socks5h`), or env-based
- **Global** or **per-domain** routing; domain rules accept exact hosts, wildcards and suffixes
- Three safety guarantees that configuration cannot loosen (below)

---

dsh-model-proxy README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add github:recyvan/dsh-model-proxy
```

Restart DSH afterwards — the host half loads inside the harness process.

Requires **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 or newer** and **Node 22.19+** (the floor the harness itself
declares in `engines`). The settings page is generated by the host from the
plugin's `Config` schema (`0.2.x` removed the `settings` service and the client-side
`settingsScope` service), so older harnesses are rejected at install time.

dsh-model-proxy README · Upgrading from 1.x：Nothing to do by hand: on first start after the upgrade the plugin converts old settings
in memory and says so on the settings page. Two conversions matter — `enabled: false`
becomes `mode: 'off'` (so a proxy you had turned off does not silently come back), and a
comma-separated domain list becomes a proper list. Press **Save** once when the page asks;
otherwise the conversion is redone, visibly, on every start.

---

dsh-model-proxy README · Configure：| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Mode | `rule` (recommended) / `system` / `custom` / `off` |
| Proxy protocol | http / https / socks5 / socks5h / socks4 |
| Proxy address | `socks5h://127.0.0.1:7890`, or just `127.0.0.1:7890` (scheme filled in from the protocol field) |
| Proxy only these domains | empty = built-in preset; otherwise one entry per chip (`*.openai.com`, `.aiplatform.googleapis.com`), added with Enter or **Add** |
| Exclude domains | always direct, highest priority (same chip editor) |
dsh-model-proxy README · Configure：Changes take effect on the next request — no restart.

dsh-model-proxy README · Three common setups：**A. Clash / V2Ray on `127.0.0.1:7890`, overseas APIs only**
Mode = `rule`, protocol = `http`, address = `127.0.0.1:7890`, leave the domain list empty.
The preset sends OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / xAI / Groq / OpenRouter and similar through
the proxy, and keeps DeepSeek, DashScope, Zhipu, Kimi and other mainland providers direct.

dsh-model-proxy README · Three common setups：**B. Follow the Windows system proxy**
Mode = `system`. The plugin re-reads
`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings` every 30 s and follows
changes made in Windows.

**C. Everything through the proxy, a few exceptions**
Mode = `custom`, fill the address, list the exceptions under "Exclude domains".

dsh-model-proxy README · Notes for overseas APIs from mainland China：- **DNS poisoning**: prefer `socks5h` (DNS resolved by the proxy), or let your proxy client
  take over DNS.
- **Plaintext `http` is refused by default** — an API key must not travel over a proxy in
  clear text. Tick the option on the settings page if you really need it.
- The proxy must listen on loopback; enable the local/LAN listener in your proxy client.

---
section: Notes for overseas APIs from mainland China

text:
dsh-model-proxy README · Verify：1. The settings page shows live status: `path A · exit route · N rules · proxied x / direct y`.
2. `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dsh-model-proxy/status` returns the same snapshot as JSON
   (loopback / same-origin only).
3. In a source checkout: `npm test` (= `node test/run-all.mjs`). The suite ships with the
   repository, not with the npm package, and needs no install — it resolves the host's own
   `undici` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` from your DSH profile (or `DSH_HOME`).

---
dsh-model-proxy README · Safety guarantees：These hold regardless of configuration, and are what the rules engine checks first:

dsh-model-proxy README · Safety guarantees：1. **Forced direct** — loopback, private ranges (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`,
   `169.254/16`, `fc00::/7` — `localhost` and `.local`/`.lan`/`.internal` style names never go
   through a proxy. User rules can add entries but cannot remove these.
2. **Plaintext gate** — a model request that is not `https` is rejected before any socket is
   opened, unless the option is explicitly enabled (the page then shows a standing warning).
3. **Data minimisation** — the plugin passes request and response bodies through as streams;
   it never parses them, never writes them to disk, and never reads `Authorization` or any
   provider API key. Default logging records the exit id and error class only — no hostnames,
   no paths, no bodies.

dsh-model-proxy README · Safety guarantees：A failed exit falls back to **direct**, never to another exit: silently moving traffic to a
different exit would change the outbound identity without the user noticing. The fallback is
logged and shown on the settings page, so a degraded state is visible rather than silent.

---

dsh-model-proxy README · Development：```
lib/index.js       Cordis host entry — the only file that touches the harness API
lib/client.js      settings page (`__ModuleLoader__` browser entry)
lib/core/*         pure logic, no harness dependency, independently testable
test/run-all.mjs   test suite: pure-logic groups, then entry-file smoke tests

dsh-model-proxy README · Development：`undici` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` are both **peers** — the harness already ships them,
and installing a second copy would mean two dispatcher/`Schema` instances. The `devDependencies`
entries exist only so `npm test` can run outside DSH; the suite itself prefers the host's copies.

The same suite runs on GitHub Actions for every push (`.github/workflows/test.yml`, Node 22 and 24):
install the two dev dependencies, `node --check` each file under `lib/`, then `npm test`.

---

dsh-model-proxy README · Limitations：- Covers requests issued through **`fetch`** — in practice every model request, plus any
  other `fetch` traffic whose domain you add to the proxy list. `transport: websocket` streaming
  and provider native-SDK channels (e.g. Amazon Bedrock) do not pass through `fetch` and cannot be
  proxied here — use the harness's built-in environment-variable proxy for those. Web page
  fetching is in the same category: the harness's fetch tool builds its own `undici` agent, so
  domain rules never see it.
- Routing is by **domain**. A domain that serves both a model API and other traffic sends all
  of it through the proxy; list such domains under "Exclude domains".
- Proxy credentials can only be embedded in the proxy address (`http://user:pass@host:port`),
  which stores them in plain text in settings. Prefer letting the proxy accept loopback
  connections without authentication.
- Proxy **chains** are supported to any depth (each hop's CONNECT is relayed through the previous
  one, in configuration order). Every hop is a real hop: the chain test suite drives three
  CONNECT stubs and asserts which port each one dialled.

dsh-model-proxy README · Verify the connection：The settings page has a **Test proxy** button. It sends one real request through the currently
configured exit and reports latency, HTTP status and a failure class — never the hostname or the
response body. This answers the question the diagnostics page cannot: *is it the proxy, or
something else?*

---

dsh-model-proxy README · Uninstall：```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> remove dsh-model-proxy
dsh --profile <your-profile>
```

After removal DSH is fully direct again — no configuration residue, no listening port.
